match.reason: The closest bank point, Community health resources, covers general services such as GPs and helplines and the barriers to reaching them, but it does not teach that youth-specific local services like headspace and youth centres support every dimension of youth health, so it is not the same idea.

draft.title: Local services for young people
card: Local services are community supports that young people can reach near where they live or study. Examples are headspace, school wellbeing staff and youth centres.
headspace
a service for people aged 12 to 25. It offers support with mental health, physical and sexual health, alcohol and other drugs, and work and study.
School wellbeing staff
people such as school counsellors and wellbeing coordinators. They support students at school and can link them to services outside it.
Youth centres
places for young people to meet, join activities and talk to youth workers. This supports social health and can help with other needs too.
draft.remember: Local services can support physical, social, emotional, mental and intellectual health.

a.q: Which description best fits a local service for young people?
opts: A community support young people can reach near home
A hospital ward that only treats serious physical injuries
A website that gives health advice from around the world
A government payment that helps families with living costs
a.why: Local services are community supports close to where young people live or study. A hospital ward is a health service, but it does not match the card's idea of a local support for all dimensions of health.
a.clue: Think about where young people can reach it.

b.q: Priya, 16, has been skipping her swimming club and feels lonely and flat since moving suburbs. Which local service could support both her social and emotional health?
opts: A youth centre with activities and youth workers to talk to
A school timetable that lists the sports on offer
A fitness app that counts her steps each day
A pharmacy that sells over-the-counter medicines
b.why: A youth centre lets Priya meet people, which supports social health, and talk to a youth worker, which supports emotional health. A step-counting app mostly targets physical activity and gives no one to talk to.
b.clue: Which option offers both people to meet and a person to talk to?

a.best: A community support young people can reach near home

b.best: A youth centre with activities and youth workers to talk to

proposal.title: Local services for young people
card: Local services are community supports that young people can reach near where they live or study. Each one supports different dimensions of health: physical, social, emotional, mental and spiritual.
headspace
a service for people aged 12 to 25. It offers support with mental health, physical and sexual health, alcohol and other drugs, and work and study.
School wellbeing staff
people such as school counsellors and wellbeing coordinators. They support students' mental and emotional health at school and can link them to services outside it.
Youth centres
places for young people to meet, join activities and talk to youth workers. Making friends supports social health, and feeling you belong supports spiritual health.
proposal.remember: No one service does everything. Between them, local services can cover every dimension of youth health.

a.q: Which statement about headspace is correct?
opts: It supports physical health as well as mental health
It only helps young people with mental health
It is a service for adults aged over 25
It is a youth centre run by school wellbeing staff
a.why: headspace offers support with physical and sexual health, alcohol and other drugs, and work and study, as well as mental health. Many students think it covers mental health only, but its support is much broader.
a.clue: Look at the full list of what it offers.

b.q: Priya, 16, joins a weekly activity at a youth centre. She makes friends and starts to feel she belongs in her new suburb. Which dimensions does this most clearly support?
opts: Social and spiritual health
Mental and spiritual health
Physical and mental health
Emotional and physical health
b.why: Making friends builds social health, and a sense of belonging is part of spiritual health. Mental and spiritual is tempting, but belonging and friendship do not mainly concern how she thinks and processes information.
b.clue: Which dimension includes a sense of belonging?
